figures.caption: Sheaf Message Passing Neural Network (SheafMPNN). Neighbourhood update at node $0$ (red), with neighbouring nodes in blue. (Left) A standard MPNN computes messages $m_{0i}$ (green) from neighbouring node states and aggregates them at node $0$. (Right) A SheafMPNN transports both endpoint representations into the shared edge stalk $\mathcal{F}(e_{0i})$ (boxes) through restriction maps (dashed grey arrows). The function $\psi$ computes their interaction, and the resulting message is pulled back through ℱ0​⊴​e0​i⊤ and aggregated at node $0$ (solid black arrows).
figures.headline: Sheaf message passing transports both endpoint states into a shared edge stalk before computing messages, unlike a standard MPNN.
citing_sentences: Figure 1 illustrates the distinction from standard message passing.

abstract: Standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) implicitly assume that neighboring nodes share the same feature space, which contributes to oversmoothing and poor performance on heterophilic graphs. Sheaf Neural Networks (SNNs) remove this assumption by giving each node and edge its own vector space and learning restriction maps that transform features as they move between neighbors. These maps define a sheaf Laplacian that drives diffusion over the graph, but existing implementations often assemble it explicitly as a global sparse block matrix, which adds memory and computational overhead and can hinder scalability. In this paper, we introduce Sheaf-MPNN, a PyTorch Geometric library that reformulates sheaf diffusion as local incidence-wise transport and aggregation, eliminating the need to construct the global Laplacian. Sheaf-MPNN implements fifteen families of SNNs under a unified message-passing framework, each supporting both homogeneous and heterogeneous graphs, and directed and undirected settings, with diagonal, general, orthogonal, and low-rank restriction maps and attention-based predictors. We further provide a unified benchmarking suite covering node- and graph-level tasks, heterogeneous graph learning, and computational efficiency, enabling systematic and reproducible comparisons across architectures. We establish theoretical equivalence between these message-passing formulations and their original counterparts and identify the architectural mechanisms needed to preserve their propagation dynamics. This unified perspective provides a principled foundation for implementing, comparing, and extending sheaf-based architectures within standard graph learning frameworks. Source code is available at https://github.com/alessioborgi/sheaf-mpnn.

sections.body: Sheaf Neural Networks (SNNs) give each node and edge its own vector space and learn restriction maps that move features into a shared edge space. Existing implementations assemble the global sheaf Laplacian as a sparse block matrix, which adds memory and computation cost. The authors present Sheaf-MPNN, a PyTorch Geometric library that computes sheaf propagation through local incidence-wise transport and aggregation without building that matrix. It implements 15 families of SNNs, with homogeneous and heterogeneous variants, directed and undirected settings, and diagonal, general, orthogonal, or low-rank restriction maps. The paper states theoretical equivalence between these message-passing forms and the original models. The authors note that practical efficiency depends on implementation and must be measured empirically.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Sheaf networks assemble a global sparse operator, and the authors propose local message passing instead.

sections.body: This section defines cellular sheaves on an undirected graph and rewrites the sheaf Laplacian as a local sum over incident edges. Each node state passes through a channel-mixing map. Each edge then combines the transported endpoint states with a function psi, and the resulting message is pulled back through the restriction map and aggregated at the node. Sheaf diffusion is recovered by taking psi as the difference with sum aggregation. Identity restrictions and identity pre-transforms recover standard message-passing networks. Directed propagation needs explicit incoming-arc aggregation, because an undirected edge gives transposed cross blocks rather than independent directional operators. The stated cost for transport and aggregation is O(|E| d^2 f), excluding map prediction and normalization.
sections.heading: Sheaf Message Passing in a Nutshell
sections.headline: Sheaf message passing recovers sheaf diffusion and standard message-passing networks as special cases of one general update.

sections.body: Sheaf-MPNN is built on PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric. It provides reusable sheaf message-passing layers and end-to-end model wrappers behind one interface. The section gives a node-classification example that uses orthogonal Neural Sheaf Diffusion. A sheaf command-line tool runs reproducible experiments across more than 20 datasets, performs Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization, and compares computational efficiency against reference implementations. The package structure, model interfaces, and experimental tooling are described in Appendix C.
sections.heading: Library Design and Usage
sections.headline: Sheaf-MPNN exposes sheaf layers and end-to-end models through one PyTorch Geometric interface with a command-line tool.

sections.body: General frameworks such as PyTorch Geometric and DGL provide message passing but no native cellular sheaves. TopoX supports higher-order topological domains, including operator-based sheaf models. Existing sheaf neural network implementations by Bodnar et al., Barbero et al., and Braithwaite et al. mainly target individual architectures and often rely on explicit sheaf-Laplacian assembly. The section positions Sheaf-MPNN as a reusable, Laplacian-free message-passing implementation across a broad family of sheaf neural networks. It adds unified benchmarking tools and theoretical equivalence results.
sections.heading: Related Software
sections.headline: Existing sheaf implementations usually cover single architectures and rely on explicitly assembled Laplacians.

sections.body: Sheaf-MPNN is publicly available on GitHub under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license. The release includes documentation and tutorial notebooks that accompany the code. Appendix C gives implementation details, supported architectures, and experimental configurations. The repository location is given in the abstract of the paper, so readers can find the source code there. The section makes no further claims about the software beyond its availability and licensing terms.
sections.heading: Availability
sections.headline: The library is public under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license, with documentation and tutorial notebooks.

sections.body: A primer defines cellular sheaves and the sheaf Laplacian. It explains the Neural Sheaf Diffusion update, which predicts restriction maps from endpoint features. A literature survey groups work into how sheaves are obtained and how signals propagate on them. It notes two recent studies, one finding the fixed identity sheaf competitive and one finding that SNNs do not surpass the strongest baselines. Table 4 lists the options of NSDModel beyond its core dimensions. The experiment tool offers run, splits, sweep, and benchmark commands. Sweeps use an Optuna TPE sampler and median pruner and re-evaluate the best configuration over ten seeds or folds. The environment pins Python 3.13, PyTorch 2.8.0, and Lightning 2.6.0. The paper states that it reports neither test coverage nor numerical parity with reference implementations.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix covers sheaf background, the Sheaf Neural Network literature, model options, experiment tooling, and reproducibility.
